hero.headline: Trump Administration Discussing Government Stake in AI Companies
hero.body:
The Trump administration is exploring the possibility of acquiring equity stakes in leading artificial intelligence companies as part of a profit-sharing arrangement with the federal government, according to multiple reports. President Trump has confirmed these discussions and indicated he will meet with AI executives next week to discuss the proposal.

The potential arrangement would grant the federal government ownership positions in major AI firms, including OpenAI, in exchange for government support of their operations. Trump framed the concept as a mechanism for taxpayers to benefit from companies that receive government assistance or utilize public resources. The administration has been actively discussing such an arrangement with OpenAI, according to CNBC reporting.

The proposal comes after Senator Bernie Sanders published an opinion piece in The New York Times proposing that artificial intelligence should be classified as a public resource. Sanders argued that American citizens should own stakes in AI companies, sparking broader discussion about who benefits from advances in AI technology development.

Next week's meetings will bring together Trump administration officials and top AI company leaders to examine how government investment and profit-sharing could work in practice. According to Politico, the discussions center on how the federal government might obtain equity stakes in exchange for infrastructure support, regulatory accommodations, or other assistance related to AI development.

This approach represents a significant shift from historical American industrial policy, which typically steers clear of direct government ownership stakes in private technology companies. Proponents of the plan argue that AI development has depended substantially on publicly funded research, government-provided computing infrastructure, and regulatory frameworks that justify public equity ownership. Those with reservations have raised concerns about potential government interference in private enterprise and the precedent that federal ownership of commercial technology firms could establish.

The rationale for government involvement reflects arguments that AI companies benefit considerably from public investment and resources. Supporters maintain that this justifies compensation to taxpayers through equity participation and profit-sharing arrangements.

The upcoming meetings are expected to clarify whether the administration intends to pursue formal legislation or executive action to establish such a program. The discussions may also address how government stakes would be valued, managed, and structured to ensure effective oversight and appropriate returns for the public.

The proposal raises several unanswered questions about implementation. Issues such as how the government would exercise its ownership rights, what voting power these stakes would provide, and how profits would be distributed remain unclear. The mechanics of determining which companies would be eligible for such arrangements and how government support would be quantified also require clarification.

These developments signal the administration's willingness to experiment with unconventional approaches to economic policy regarding emerging technologies, particularly those deemed critical to national interests.

cards.headline: US shoots down Iranian drones over Strait of Hormuz as tensions escalate in Gulf
cards.body:
The US military shot down an Iranian drone that approached the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea, according to US Central Command. An F-35C fighter jet downed the Iranian Shahed-139 drone on Tuesday after it flew toward the carrier "with unclear intent," the military said.

"An F-35C fighter jet from Abraham Lincoln shot down the Iranian drone in self-defence and to protect the aircraft carrier and personnel on board," said Captain Tim Hawkins, a navy spokesperson at Central Command. No US service members were harmed and no equipment was damaged.

Iran's UN mission declined to comment on the incident. Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that connection had been lost with a drone in international waters, though the cause remained unknown. The semi-official Fars news agency claimed that an Iranian drone had completed a "surveillance mission in international waters."

In a separate incident on Tuesday, Iranian Revolutionary Guards harassed a US-flagged merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. "Two IRGC boats and an Iranian Mohajer drone approached M/V Stena Imperative at high speeds and threatened to board and seize the tanker," Hawkins said.

The drone incident occurred as diplomats worked to arrange nuclear negotiations between the two countries. Donald Trump said that with US warships heading toward Iran, "bad things" would likely happen unless a deal could be reached. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian responded by instructing his country's foreign minister to "pursue fair and equitable negotiations" with the US, marking the first clear signal that Tehran wanted to negotiate with Washington.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed that Trump envoy Steve Witkoff still plans to hold talks with Iranian officials later in the week despite the drone incident. However, Iran's foreign ministry said consultations were still underway on the venue, with reports suggesting Tehran preferred Oman over Turkey and wanted discussions limited to nuclear-related issues.

Pezeshkian's announcement represented a significant shift for the reformist president, who had previously told Iranians that the country's turmoil had gone beyond his control. The statement indicated support from Iran's supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, for negotiations that the 86-year-old cleric had previously dismissed.

The Lincoln carrier strike group represents the most visible aspect of a US military buildup in the Middle East following a violent crackdown against anti-government demonstrations in Iran last month, the deadliest domestic unrest since the 1979 revolution. Trump has demanded Tehran make nuclear concessions and deployed a flotilla to Iran's coast. He said last week that Iran was "seriously talking."

cards.headline: Israel strikes southern Lebanon after ordering village evacuations
cards.teaser: Israel conducted strikes in southern Lebanon after ordering residents of nine villages to evacuate.
cards.body:
Israeli forces struck targets in southern Lebanon following evacuation orders for nine villages in the region. The military action occurred despite a new ceasefire agreement announced by the United States on Wednesday night.

Hezbollah has rejected the ceasefire terms. In a separate incident, a UN peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when mortar fire struck the UNIFIL peacekeeping mission in southeastern Lebanon.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Post Worst Daily Drop of 2026 on Jobs Data
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 fell more than 2.6 percent, ending nine weeks of gains, while the Nasdaq dropped 4 percent in its worst day since April 2025.
cards.body:
U.S. stock markets suffered their sharpest declines of the year on Friday following a stronger-than-expected jobs report. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 695 points, while the S&P 500 dropped more than 2.6 percent and the Nasdaq plunged 4 percent. The losses marked the biggest percentage drops for the major indexes since 2025 and ended a nine-week winning streak.

The selloff centered on technology stocks, particularly AI and semiconductor companies, as investors reassessed interest rate expectations. Treasury yields jumped following the jobs data, which suggested continued economic strength. The strong employment numbers increased expectations that the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates, prompting traders to flee high-valuation tech stocks.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigations into California elections, sends prosecutor to Los Angeles
cards.teaser: The US attorney's office announced multiple investigations into California's elections and dispatched a federal prosecutor to observe ballot counting in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
The US Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to Los Angeles on Friday to observe ballot processing as the state continues counting votes in several races, including the gubernatorial primary. The move comes as former President Trump has made claims that California Democrats are "rigging" election results, allegations that state officials have rejected.

California's mail-in voting system typically requires days or weeks to complete the count. The delay in results has fueled misinformation about election integrity, with Trump repeatedly accusing the state of cheating despite experts noting that slow ballot counting is standard for the state's primary elections.

cards.headline: Whistleblower alleges DOGE plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead
cards.teaser: A plan to incorrectly designate millions of living Americans as deceased was part of an immigration enforcement initiative, according to a whistleblower allegation.
cards.body:
A whistleblower has alleged that a plan developed as part of immigration enforcement efforts would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead in government databases.

The claim raises concerns about the potential impact on government records and the individuals who would have been incorrectly listed as deceased. Being wrongly marked as dead in federal databases can affect access to benefits, financial accounts, and other critical services. The whistleblower's disclosure did not specify whether the plan was implemented or remained in the proposal stage.

cards.headline: Putin declines meeting with Zelenskyy over Ukraine war
cards.teaser: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he sees no reason to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
cards.body:
Vladimir Putin rejected Zelenskyy's public offer to hold face-to-face talks aimed at ending the Ukraine conflict. Speaking at the St. Petersburg economic forum, Putin said he saw "no point" in such a meeting and described Zelenskyy's open letter as rude, refusing even to use his name.

Putin reaffirmed Russia's commitment to achieving its war objectives, including seizing all of the eastern Donbas region. At the forum, business and political elites acknowledged Russia faced a choice between halting the conflict or accepting further sacrifices—a choice Putin's response appeared to answer in favor of continuing the war.

cards.headline: Protests grow in Albania over Kushner-linked resort project
cards.teaser: Demonstrations have escalated in Albania over a planned luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner near a protected wetland.
cards.body:
Thousands of demonstrators have taken to the streets of Tirana this week to oppose a $1.6 billion luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner. The project is located in an environmentally sensitive Mediterranean area that hosts over 200 bird species, including flamingos and Dalmatian pelicans.

Construction has begun on the site, with workers erecting concrete fencing topped with barbed wire. The development has sparked public outrage over environmental damage and concerns about a lack of political transparency in the deal's approval process.

cards.headline: France opens probe into Israeli treatment of Gaza flotilla activists
cards.teaser: French authorities launched an investigation into alleged abuse of activists detained by Israel while attempting to reach Gaza.
cards.body:
France has opened a formal investigation into the treatment of pro-Palestinian flotilla activists detained by Israeli forces. The activists were intercepted while attempting to reach Gaza by sea and taken into Israeli custody.

Those detained have alleged they experienced abuse while held by Israeli authorities. Israeli officials have denied the mistreatment allegations. The investigation was initiated following formal complaints filed by French citizens who participated in the flotilla operation.

cards.headline: EU signals Montenegro could join bloc by 2028
cards.teaser: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Montenegro is within reach of EU membership by 2028.
cards.body:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Montenegro is "within reach" of EU membership by 2028 following a Balkans summit. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced the EU would initiate the integration of Western Balkan nations, signaling an effort to accelerate the membership timeline for the region.

The push reflects EU strategy to counter Russian and Chinese influence in the Balkans. Montenegro has been a candidate for years, but the accession process has experienced repeated delays. All EU member states must approve new members, and candidates must meet strict economic and governance standards before formally joining.

cards.headline: Astronauts return to ISS after sheltering during leak repair
cards.teaser: Five astronauts returned to their normal stations on the International Space Station after sheltering during a Russian repair attempt.
cards.body:
NASA ordered five astronauts aboard the International Space Station to prepare for possible evacuation after Russian specialists detected two air leaks in the Zveda module's transfer chamber. The leaks were discovered while pressurizing the chamber during routine operations.

The crew moved to safe-haven areas while Russian personnel worked on repairs. NASA subsequently cleared the astronauts to return to their regular activities as the repair work progressed.

hero.headline: Park ranger dies after falling into crevasse on Denali
hero.body:
A National Park Service ranger died after falling into a crevasse on Denali, the park service announced. The ranger was conducting a patrol on the mountain, known officially as Mount McKinley, when the accident occurred. The death marks the fourth fatality on the mountain this climbing season.

The ranger worked for the National Park Service and was from Washington state, according to reports. The fall happened during routine patrol operations on the Alaska mountain, which stands as the highest peak in North America at more than 20,000 feet. Crevasses are deep cracks in glacial ice that pose one of the most serious hazards to climbers and mountaineers.

Denali's climbing season typically runs from late spring through early summer, when weather conditions are most favorable. Despite this, the mountain remains extremely dangerous, with unpredictable weather, high altitude, and glacial terrain creating constant risks. Park rangers regularly patrol climbing routes to assist mountaineers, monitor conditions, and conduct rescues when necessary.

The climbing season has proven particularly deadly this year, with three other fatalities already recorded before this incident. Rangers who work on Denali undergo specialized training in mountaineering, wilderness medicine, and high-altitude rescue operations. Their patrols are considered essential for climber safety, though the work itself carries significant risk.

The National Park Service has not released additional details about the circumstances of the fall or the recovery operation. Denali National Park attracts more than 1,000 climbers each year who attempt to reach the summit, with success rates varying widely depending on weather and conditions. The mountain's extreme environment and technical climbing requirements make it one of the most challenging climbs in the world, even for experienced mountaineers and trained professionals.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigations into California elections, sends prosecutor to Los Angeles
cards.teaser: The US attorney's office announced multiple investigations into California's elections and dispatched a federal prosecutor to observe ballot counting in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
The US Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to Los Angeles on Friday to observe ballot processing as the state continues counting votes in several races, including the gubernatorial primary. The move comes as former President Trump has made claims that California Democrats are "rigging" election results, allegations that state officials have rejected.

California's mail-in voting system typically requires days or weeks to complete the count. The delay in results has fueled misinformation about election integrity, with Trump repeatedly accusing the state of cheating despite experts noting that slow ballot counting is standard for the state's primary elections.

cards.headline: Virginia man sentenced to life in prison for plotting wife's murder with au pair
cards.teaser: Brendan Banfield received a life sentence for plotting with his family's au pair to kill his wife and a stranger during an affair.
cards.body:
Brendan Banfield, a former IRS law enforcement officer, was sentenced to life in prison without parole for the murders of his wife Christine and a man named Joseph Ryan. Banfield claimed he shot Ryan in self-defense after discovering him attacking his wife on February 24, 2023. However, prosecutors presented evidence that Banfield and the family's Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhães, orchestrated the killings as part of a scheme to eliminate Christine.

According to the prosecution, Ryan was lured to the couple's Virginia home as a fall guy in the murder plot. Banfield's affair with the au pair was a key factor in the case, with prosecutors arguing the scheme was designed to facilitate their relationship.

cards.headline: Appeals court hears arguments on Trump White House ballroom project
cards.teaser: The Justice Department argued in court that presidents have broad authority over federal property, defending the White House ballroom construction.
cards.body:
The Trump administration asked the DC Circuit Court of Appeals to overturn a lower court decision blocking construction of a $400 million ballroom on the White House grounds. A Justice Department lawyer argued that no court has authority to halt the project, claiming only Congress could stop it. The administration contends that courts cannot intervene in decisions about federal property under presidential control.

The ballroom project involves demolishing the White House's East Wing. While the legal dispute continues between DC preservationists and the White House, construction of a secure underground bunker at the site has been permitted to proceed. The project has grown substantially in both scale and budget over the past year.

cards.headline: Trump visits Wisconsin farmers, says he could be home watching television
cards.teaser: The president traveled to farm country in Wisconsin but told the audience he could be at home watching television instead.
cards.body:
President Trump visited Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin, to meet with farmers in the state's agricultural region. During the appearance, he told the crowd he could be home watching television, and also praised fountains in Washington during his pitch to the farm community.

The visit comes as farmers face economic pressure from tariffs and high prices. Farm country has traditionally been a strong base of support for Trump, though his trade policies have created difficulties for agricultural producers who depend on export markets and are affected by retaliatory tariffs from other countries.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra advances to November runoff in California governor race
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra secured the top spot on California's gubernatorial ballot, with his November opponent still undetermined.
cards.body:
Democrat Xavier Becerra has clinched the top spot in California's gubernatorial primary and will advance to November's general election. The former Health and Human Services Secretary pulled off a come-from-behind victory in one of California's most turbulent campaign seasons.

With millions of ballots still being counted, Becerra's November opponent remains to be determined. He could face fellow Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist who supports universal healthcare and higher taxes on billionaires, or Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality who received Donald Trump's endorsement.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes in Gulf waters
cards.teaser: The US military struck Iranian drones and radar sites, and Tehran responded by targeting American bases in Kuwait and Bahrain.
cards.body:
The US military struck Iranian drones and radar sites in the Gulf region. Iran responded by targeting US military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, marking another escalation in the fragile ceasefire that took effect in April.

Both nations claim advantage in the exchange, yet analysts suggest neither side is achieving its objectives. The ceasefire has prevented full-scale war but remains unstable, with repeated flare-ups raising concerns about regional stability and the future of diplomatic efforts.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Post Worst Daily Drop of 2026 on Jobs Data
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 fell more than 2.6 percent, ending nine weeks of gains, while the Nasdaq dropped 4 percent in its worst day since April 2025.
cards.body:
U.S. stock markets suffered their sharpest declines of the year on Friday following a stronger-than-expected jobs report. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 695 points, while the S&P 500 dropped more than 2.6 percent and the Nasdaq plunged 4 percent. The losses marked the biggest percentage drops for the major indexes since 2025 and ended a nine-week winning streak.

The selloff centered on technology stocks, particularly AI and semiconductor companies, as investors reassessed interest rate expectations. Treasury yields jumped following the jobs data, which suggested continued economic strength. The strong employment numbers increased expectations that the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates, prompting traders to flee high-valuation tech stocks.

cards.headline: Google Agrees to Pay SpaceX Nearly $1 Billion Monthly for Cloud Computing
cards.teaser: The deal totals approximately $30 billion and will provide Google with AI computing power at SpaceX data centers.
cards.body:
Google has agreed to pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing capacity at data centers operated by xAI. The deal is valued at approximately $30 billion, making it one of the largest cloud computing contracts in the technology industry.

A Google representative attributed the deal to unexpected demand for the company's recently launched AI products. The arrangement will support AI workloads, reflecting the substantial infrastructure requirements needed to train and operate large-scale artificial intelligence systems.

cards.headline: States Preparing Lawsuit to Block Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros
cards.teaser: Multiple U.S. states are developing antitrust litigation to prevent the merger of the two major entertainment companies.
cards.body:
Several U.S. states are preparing a lawsuit to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros., according to Reuters. California is expected to decide soon whether it will join the legal effort to prevent the merger. The states are citing antitrust concerns about the combination of two major entertainment companies.

Paramount has pushed back against opposition to the deal, with company lawyers claiming some opponents hold antisemitic views, according to Variety. Paramount also filed motions seeking to dismiss existing lawsuits challenging the transaction, calling them a clumsy attempt to politicize antitrust litigation. The state attorneys general have not yet formally filed their complaint.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Falls to $60,000, Lowest Level Since October 2024
cards.teaser: The cryptocurrency tumbled after strong jobs data increased expectations for interest rate hikes, while a bug in Zcash added pressure.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 on Friday, marking its lowest price since October 2024. The decline coincided with a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report, which raised expectations that the Federal Reserve might increase interest rates. A technical issue with Zcash, another cryptocurrency, also pressured the broader market.

The selling reflects a wider shift in investor sentiment. Cryptocurrencies have faced headwinds as investors rotated toward artificial intelligence stocks and major initial public offerings. Some analysts warn against dismissing Bitcoin's long-term prospects despite the recent losses and market skepticism from crypto bears.

cards.headline: Semiconductor Stocks Continue Selloff After Broadcom Results
cards.teaser: Intel, AMD, and Micron shares fell as chip stocks extended losses triggered by Broadcom's quarterly results.
cards.body:
Semiconductor stocks extended their selloff on Friday, with Broadcom and Intel leading declines across the chip sector. The losses began after Broadcom released quarterly results that sparked broader concerns about the semiconductor industry. Intel, AMD, and Micron all saw their shares drop, though they trimmed some losses later in the session.

Bloomberg reported that the chip stock slump rekindled Wall Street's buy-the-dip trading pattern, with some investors viewing the decline as a potential entry point. CNBC noted that traders believe other sectors could now lead the market higher, reducing reliance on technology stocks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average reached a record high even as tech stocks tumbled, suggesting rotation into other sectors.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Tops List of Highest Paid CEOs as Compensation Gap Widens
cards.teaser: Executive pay is accelerating while rank-and-file worker wages lag, expanding the compensation divide in corporate America.
cards.body:
Elon Musk leads the ranking of highest paid chief executives, according to new compensation data. The report shows that executive pay continues to accelerate across corporate America while wages for typical workers grow at a slower pace, creating a widening gap between top executives and their employees.

Labor advocates and policymakers have raised concerns about this disparity, pointing out that executive compensation has grown disproportionately compared to worker wages in recent years.

hero.headline: Reid Hoffman Leaves Microsoft Board to Focus on AI Drug Discovery Startup
hero.body:
Reid Hoffman has stepped down from Microsoft's board of directors after a decade to concentrate on his artificial intelligence drug discovery startup, Manus. The LinkedIn co-founder announced his departure to dedicate full attention to the health technology venture.

Hoffman joined Microsoft's board following LinkedIn's acquisition by the tech giant. During his tenure, he participated in overseeing the company's strategic direction through a period of significant growth and transformation in cloud computing and artificial intelligence. His board service proved financially rewarding over the ten-year span.

Manus represents Hoffman's latest entrepreneurial effort, applying artificial intelligence to pharmaceutical research and drug development. The startup aims to accelerate the discovery process for new medications by using machine learning and computational methods to identify promising drug candidates. This approach could reduce the time and cost traditionally required to bring new treatments to market.

Hoffman's decision reflects a broader trend of technology investors and executives moving into healthcare and life sciences sectors. Artificial intelligence applications in drug discovery have attracted substantial venture capital investment in recent years, as the technology shows potential to transform how pharmaceutical companies identify and develop new therapies. The field combines computational biology, chemistry, and machine learning to predict which molecular compounds might effectively treat specific diseases.

The transition marks a shift for Hoffman from a governance role at one of the world's largest technology companies to an operational position at an early-stage startup. His departure from Microsoft's board creates a vacancy that the company will need to fill. Hoffman remains a prominent figure in Silicon Valley venture capital and technology circles, and his move to focus exclusively on Manus signals confidence in the startup's mission and market opportunity.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy to Conclude with Revelation in 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix revealed the final installment in its Final Fantasy VII remake series will launch in spring 2027.
cards.body:
Square Enix officially announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final installment of its remake trilogy during Summer Game Fest. The game will launch simultaneously across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in spring 2027.

The remake series began with Final Fantasy VII Remake in 2020, followed by Rebirth. Revelation will bring the reimagined saga of the 1997 PlayStation classic to its conclusion.

cards.headline: Guild Wars 3 Announced for PC and PlayStation 5
cards.teaser: ArenaNet revealed Guild Wars 3 at Summer Game Fest, with a beta test planned for fall 2027.
cards.body:
The developer announced Guild Wars 3 as a modern evolution of the massively multiplayer online role-playing game franchise. The new title will launch on PC and PlayStation 5, marking an expansion from the previous game's PC-only availability.

ArenaNet plans to conduct a beta test in fall 2027 before the full release. The announcement raises questions about the future of Guild Wars 2, which has maintained an active player base since its 2012 launch. Guild Wars 3 represents the first numbered sequel in the series in over a decade.

cards.headline: Capcom Announces Resident Evil: Code Veronica Remake for 2027
cards.teaser: Capcom revealed a remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica, titled Resident Evil: Veronica, set to launch in 2027.
cards.body:
Capcom revealed a remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica during Summer Game Fest. The project continues the publisher's effort to reimagine classic entries from the survival horror franchise, following remakes of Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4. The remake launches in 2027.

The original Code Veronica debuted in 2000 on Dreamcast before expanding to additional platforms. The game centered on Claire Redfield's quest to find her brother Chris while introducing new mechanics to the franchise.

cards.headline: Hitman Classic Trilogy Remastered Coming to Consoles in 2027
cards.teaser: IO Interactive announced remastered versions of the first three Hitman games for modern consoles.
cards.body:
The developer revealed the Hitman Classic Trilogy Remastered, bringing the original three games in the stealth franchise to Xbox and PlayStation 5. The collection will launch in 2027, allowing players to experience Agent 47's early missions with updated graphics and performance.

The trilogy includes Hitman: Codename 47, Hitman 2: Silent Assassin, and Hitman: Contracts. IO Interactive made the announcement during Summer Game Fest, adding to the lineup of classic game remasters revealed at the event. The original games released between 2000 and 2004 on PC and earlier console generations.

cards.headline: Stellar Blade Sequel Blood Rain Revealed in Development
cards.teaser: Shift Up announced a sequel to Stellar Blade currently in production, featuring a darker tone.
cards.body:
Shift Up unveiled Stellar Blade: Blood Rain at Summer Game Fest with a debut trailer. The sequel marks the developer's next project following the original game's PlayStation 5 release earlier this year.

Blood Rain appears to shift toward a horror-focused direction compared to the action-oriented gameplay of its predecessor. The trailer showcased visual and tonal changes that distinguish the sequel from the original science fiction title.

cards.headline: Astronauts Return to ISS After Air Leak Repair Attempt
cards.teaser: Five astronauts returned to normal operations after sheltering during a Russian repair attempt on a leaking tunnel.
cards.body:
NASA ordered five astronauts aboard the International Space Station to prepare for a possible evacuation after Russian specialists detected two air leaks in the Zvezda module's transfer chamber during a pressurization procedure. The leaks were discovered as the Russian segment's operations team worked to pressurize the chamber connecting to the ISS.

Following the detection, the crew implemented safety protocols and sheltered in other modules while repair efforts were underway. NASA subsequently authorized the astronauts to return to regular activities as the repair work was paused.

hero.headline: NBA investigating Clippers over alleged salary cap violation involving Kawhi Leonard
hero.teaser: The league has interviewed Kawhi Leonard and his business adviser as part of a probe into whether the Clippers circumvented the salary cap to compensate the star.
hero.body:
The NBA has interviewed Los Angeles Clippers star Kawhi Leonard and his business adviser as part of an investigation into allegations that the team violated salary cap rules. League investigators are examining whether the Clippers provided compensation to Leonard outside of his official contract.

The probe focuses on whether the team circumvented the salary cap, which limits how much teams can spend on player salaries. Salary cap violations can result in significant penalties for teams, including fines and loss of draft picks.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-0 NBA Finals lead after Wembanyama miss at buzzer
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 on Friday night to take a 2-0 lead in the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 on Friday night to claim a 2-0 series lead in the NBA Finals. Jalen Brunson secured the win by hitting a go-ahead free throw with 9.5 seconds remaining. The decisive moment came after Victor Wembanyama turned the ball over, and the Spurs' young center then missed a jumper at the buzzer that would have tied the game.

The one-point victory punctuated a thrilling finish between the two teams. The series now moves to New York for the next two games, giving the Knicks home-court advantage as they look to extend their commanding lead. San Antonio faces a critical juncture, needing to win on the road to keep their championship aspirations alive.

cards.headline: Iran national team receives US visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Players on Iran's World Cup team have been granted visas that will allow them to enter and compete in the United States for the tournament.
cards.body:
A U.S. official confirmed to ABC News on Friday that Iran's World Cup team players have received visas to enter the United States for the tournament. The visa approval enables the team to compete in the competition beginning in June.

Iran will play its opening match on June 16 as the World Cup takes place across venues in North America.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi could play World Cup warmups after recovering from hamstring issue
cards.teaser: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said Messi is improving from muscle fatigue in his left hamstring and could see minutes in warmup matches before the team's World Cup opener.
cards.body:
Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said Lionel Messi is improving from muscle fatigue in his left hamstring and could play some minutes in warmup matches before the World Cup. Scaloni indicated the star forward is making progress with his recovery.

Argentina begins its World Cup campaign on June 16. The team will use preparatory matches to get ready for the tournament, with Messi's potential involvement offering a significant lift to the squad as it fine-tunes its preparations.

cards.headline: FIFA reverses ban on refillable water bottles at World Cup stadiums
cards.teaser: FIFA reversed its decision to prohibit fans from bringing refillable water bottles into World Cup stadiums after facing significant criticism.
cards.body:
FIFA has reversed its decision to ban refillable water bottles at World Cup stadiums across North America following widespread criticism. The policy reversal addresses concerns about fan hydration during the June tournament, when temperatures in some host cities can be high.

The initial ban on bringing personal water bottles into the 16 stadiums drew fierce backlash from fans and observers who highlighted the importance of staying hydrated during matches in potentially hot conditions.

cards.headline: Aaron Judge says rib fracture originated from April diving catch
cards.teaser: The Yankees outfielder said the stress fracture in his right rib stems from diving for a ball in late April.
cards.body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge attributed his right rib stress fracture to a diving catch attempt in late April. The injury occurred weeks before being officially diagnosed.

Stress fractures of the rib typically require extended rest before players can resume full competition. Judge's injury has sidelined him from the Yankees lineup during the recovery period.

cards.headline: SEC commissioner dismisses talk of super league with Big Ten
cards.teaser: Greg Sankey called the notion that the SEC wants to form a super league with the Big Ten inconsistent with the truth.
cards.body:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey rejected speculation about a potential super league involving the SEC and Big Ten, calling the notion "not consistent with the truth." His comments push back against recent reports suggesting the two conferences might pursue a major restructuring of college athletics.

The dismissal comes as both the SEC and Big Ten continue reshaping their rosters through conference realignment and expansion efforts.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy Fatally Stabbed in Los Angeles; Girlfriend's Son Charged with Murder
hero.body:
Veteran character actor James Handy, 81, died after being stabbed at his home in Tarzana, Los Angeles. Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, has been arrested and charged with murder in connection with the death.

Police discovered Handy unconscious in the front yard of his Tarzana residence at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday. He had sustained multiple stab wounds to the chest. He was transported to a hospital where he was later pronounced dead.

According to the Los Angeles Police Department, a 911 caller stated: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." When officers arrived at the scene, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for." The police statement noted that Gledhill resides at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend.

Gledhill has been charged on suspicion of murder, with bail set at 2 million dollars. Murder proceedings have been temporarily paused as Gledhill undergoes a mental competency examination, according to court filings. The Los Angeles County District Attorney's office will proceed with the case pending the results of the evaluation. If Gledhill is found mentally competent to stand trial, he will face murder charges. This type of evaluation is standard procedure when questions arise about a defendant's ability to understand court proceedings or assist in their own defense.

Handy had a distinguished career spanning decades in film and television. He was known for his character roles in productions including Jumanji, Top Gun: Maverick, and Logan. His acting career began in 1977 with the television series Ryan's Hope. Throughout his career, he appeared in numerous other productions including K-911, Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. His most recent film appearance was in Top Gun: Maverick, released in 2022.

The actor was born in New York City and built a reputation for his work in character roles across multiple genres. His death has drawn attention both due to his profile in the entertainment industry and the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Authorities have not released additional details about the events leading up to the stabbing or a possible motive for the attack. The case remains under investigation by the Los Angeles Police Department and the District Attorney's office.

cards.headline: Rock Tattoo Artist Greg James Dies at 71
cards.teaser: Greg James, a tattoo artist known for his work with rock musicians, has died at age 71.
cards.body: Greg James, a tattoo artist who became known in the music industry for his work with rock performers, died at 71. James built a reputation over decades for tattooing prominent figures in the rock music scene. James was recognized within both tattoo and music communities for his distinctive style and long career.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Releases Music Video for Toy Story 5 Song Featuring Jessie
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift's song for Toy Story 5 received a music video featuring footage of the character Jessie and has broken streaming records.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift released a music video for her Toy Story 5 song centered on the character Jessie. The video features footage from the upcoming animated film and has been praised for its nostalgic tone.

In a post about the song, Swift paid tribute to Randy Newman, who created the iconic Toy Story musical world, calling him "incomparable." The track marks her return to pop country style and has achieved significant streaming success on Spotify.

cards.headline: Sean Penn Skipped Oscars to Avoid Large Gatherings, Won Best Supporting Actor
cards.teaser: Sean Penn won his third Oscar for Best Supporting Actor but did not attend the ceremony due to his aversion to large public events.
cards.body:
Sean Penn won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role in One Battle After Another at the 98th Oscars but skipped the ceremony. The actor cited mental health reasons for his absence, explaining to CNN anchor Kaitlin Collins that he avoids public gatherings with more than eight people.

Penn is also known for his firm stance against selfies and refuses to take them with anyone under any circumstances. Despite winning his third Oscar, he was not present to accept the statuette in person.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Season 8 Becomes Peacock's Most-Watched TV Debut
cards.teaser: The eighth season of Love Island USA set a viewership record for Peacock, with 824 million minutes watched in its first three episodes.
cards.body:
Season 8 of Love Island USA has set a new record as Peacock's most-watched debut for an original television season. The season launched on June 2 and has released three episodes, accumulating 824 million minutes watched.

The viewership represents a significant 74 percent increase from the previous season. Mobile devices accounted for 23 percent of total viewing, with audiences watching on phones and tablets rather than traditional television screens, highlighting shifting preferences in how people consume reality programming.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII: Revelation Announced as Final Game in Remake Trilogy
cards.teaser: Square Enix revealed Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the concluding title in its remake trilogy, set to launch in spring 2027.
cards.body:
Square Enix has officially announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final installment in its Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy. The game will launch in spring 2027 across PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X and S, and PC. A trailer was unveiled at Summer Game Fest Live.

This conclusion follows Final Fantasy VII Remake and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, completing the remake trilogy that reimagines the classic 1997 original.

cards.headline: Among Us Animated Series Launches on Paramount+ Without Prior Notice
cards.teaser: An animated television adaptation of Among Us became available on Paramount+ with all 10 episodes released simultaneously.
cards.body:
The animated Among Us television series launched on Paramount+ with all 10 episodes available for streaming. The announcement came as a surprise during Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, where series stars Yvette Nicole Brown and Liv Hewson revealed the release.

The show is based on the popular multiplayer video game Among Us. The unexpected drop strategy meant audiences had no advance notice of the premiere date. The series was developed without a traditional marketing campaign or advance screening period.

hero.headline: Justice Department ends Trump anti-weaponization compensation fund
hero.body:
The Justice Department confirmed in a court filing Friday that the Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund will not continue. Two DOJ attorneys submitted the filing in the Eastern District of Virginia, asking the court to reject a legal challenge brought by a former federal prosecutor and others.

The fund was established to compensate individuals who claimed they were wrongly targeted by government investigations that the Trump administration characterized as politically motivated. The program faced swift legal and political opposition after its announcement last month as part of a settlement in the president's lawsuit against the IRS over the leak of his tax returns.

The backlash came from multiple directions. US District Judge Leonie Brinkema temporarily blocked the administration from transferring money from the fund after the nonprofit Democracy Forward filed a lawsuit seeking to dissolve it. Several states, including California, New York, Illinois, and Connecticut, proposed measures to tax any distributions from the fund to their residents.

The fund drew particular criticism because of its lack of oversight and secrecy. The terms did not require disclosure of how much money would be paid to whom. Administration officials acknowledged that payouts could include pardoned January 6 rioters, prompting sharp rebuke from across the political spectrum.

"Trump's nearly $2bn Maga slush fund is his most brazen act of self-dealing yet and one of the most corrupt schemes ever launched by a president," said US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, who vowed that Senate Democrats would not allow it to stand.

Even some Republicans expressed alarm. Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters that "the best way to handle it is if the administration decides to shut the fund down themselves." Former Vice President Mike Pence called the possibility of compensating rioters who assaulted police officers and vandalized the Capitol "deeply offensive."

The fund had faced questions about whether the executive branch possessed the authority to create a compensation mechanism without congressional approval. Legal experts raised concerns about the fund's structure and implementation from its inception.

The Justice Department's court filing confirms the administration's decision to discontinue the program. The filing asked the court to dismiss the legal challenge, arguing that discontinuation resolves the underlying dispute. The department did not provide details about whether any payments had already been distributed from the fund or explain what will happen to the allocated money.

The termination of the fund removes one significant element from ongoing litigation over Trump administration policies, though the court must still rule on the DOJ's motion to dismiss the case.

cards.headline: Whistleblower alleges DOGE plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead
cards.teaser: A plan to incorrectly designate millions of living Americans as deceased was part of an immigration enforcement initiative, according to a whistleblower allegation.
cards.body:
A whistleblower has alleged that a plan developed as part of immigration enforcement efforts would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead in government databases.

The claim raises concerns about the potential impact on government records and the individuals who would have been incorrectly listed as deceased. Being wrongly marked as dead in federal databases can affect access to benefits, financial accounts, and other critical services. The whistleblower's disclosure did not specify whether the plan was implemented or remained in the proposal stage.

cards.headline: Agriculture Department confirms second screwworm case in Texas
cards.teaser: The USDA confirmed a second detection of flesh-eating screwworm parasite in Texas as it works to contain the outbreak before it affects the cattle population.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed a second case of New World screwworm in Texas on Friday. The parasite was detected in a one-month-old calf in Zavala County, following testing of multiple suspected cases as authorities work to contain the outbreak.

The screwworm is a flesh-eating parasite whose larvae feed on living tissue in warm-blooded animals. Without treatment, infestations can cause severe damage or death. The USDA is focused on preventing the outbreak from spreading through the livestock population in the affected area.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra wins top position in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra clinched the top spot on California's November ballot for governor, though his challenger remains unknown.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra, former Health and Human Services Secretary, has secured the top spot in California's gubernatorial primary. He will advance to the November general election, emerging from a crowded field that included fellow Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer, as well as Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton.

Election officials are still counting millions of ballots to determine Becerra's November opponent. His challenger will either be Tom Steyer, an environmental activist who supports progressive policies including universal healthcare, or Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality endorsed by Donald Trump.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. She previously served in Congress before joining the cabinet as the first Native American cabinet secretary.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in the United States.

cards.headline: Chief of staff to Texas congressman faces firearm charges
cards.teaser: Luis Vega, chief of staff for Representative Pete Sessions, was charged with two firearm counts months after allegedly attempting to bring a weapon into the Capitol complex.
cards.body:
Luis Vega, who serves as chief of staff to Rep. Pete Sessions of Texas, was charged with two firearm-related counts in connection with an alleged incident at the U.S. Capitol complex. The charges were filed months after Vega allegedly attempted to bring a firearm into the Capitol complex in late December.

The charges against Vega were filed on a recent Wednesday, according to court documents. The incident occurred days before Christmas of the previous year. Bringing firearms into the Capitol complex is prohibited under federal law, with limited exceptions for law enforcement officers. Sessions represents a Texas district in the House of Representatives.

cards.headline: New York legislature passes data center and consumer protection bills
cards.teaser: The state Senate and Assembly passed three bills regulating data centers, surveillance pricing, and digital stalking while leaving other measures unaddressed.
cards.body:
The New York State Senate and Assembly approved three bills addressing data center regulation, surveillance pricing practices, and digital stalking. The legislation includes a moratorium on data centers and new consumer protections against certain business practices and online harassment.

The three bills now await action by Governor Kathy Hochul. The data center moratorium would temporarily halt new facilities while the state develops comprehensive regulations for the industry. The legislature did not advance other proposed measures related to environmental policy, housing, and entertainment that had been under consideration.
